english.title: Request / agree to receive / accept a financial / other advantage intending to perform improperly a function / activity
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..)

(A)_[requested]_
(B)_[agreed to receive]_
(C)_[accepted]_

a financial or other advantage, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ADVANTAGE..), intending that in consequence, a relevant function or activity, namely **(..SPECIFY THE FUNCTION OR ACTIVITY..), should be performed improperly
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 2(2) and 11 of the Bribery Act 2010.

english.notes:
(i) For bribery offences under section 2(2) of the Bribery Act 2010 see H100584, and for conspiracy of that offence H100586.
(ii) Section 2(6) of the Bribery Act 2010 provides that it does not matter if the defendant requests, agrees to receive or accepts (or is to request, agree to receive or accept) the advantage directly or through a third party. It also does not matter that the advantage is, or is to be, for the benefit of his / herself or another.
(iii) Prosecution of this offence requires the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions or the Director of the Serious Fraud Office, section 10.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 10 years imprisonment and / or a fine.Notes:
The reference to 12 months is to be read as 6 months in relation to an offence committed before the commencement of paragraph 24(2) of Schedule 22 to the Sentencing Act 2020.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Where any person other than an individual, e.g. a company, is convicted of this offence:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: A fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Noneviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
